subject: sum-to-zero constraint for fixed categorical variable

messages.author: 80b903b54c9cf4bd
messages.subject: sum-to-zero constraint for fixed categorical variable
parts:
Hi, I noticed when inla treats categorical variable, it sets the first level as reference level, which is 0. So the constraint is 

a_1 = 0

where a = (a_1, ..., a_n) are n levels of the variable.

Is that possible to tell inla add a_1 + ... + a_n = 0 as the constraint in the formular:

y ~ 1 + a

so that the interpretation of a would be the differences from the ground mean. 

Thanks,

Jiang

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] sum-to-zero constraint for fixed categorical variable
parts:
Yes, factors are handled by what model.matrix() does, and so work similarly to in lm().

To get the behaviour you describe, you can instead use an f(...,model=“iid”, constr=TRUE) random effects model and impose a sum to zero constrain there (and optionally fix the precision parameter, to mimic the behaviour of a regular factor covariate).

Finn

Let a be a factor

… f(a, model=“iid”, constr=T, hyper=list(prec=list(initial=-4,fixed=TRUE))))
